data.title: Anticipatory metabolic regulation drives the distinct and improved metabolic state of caloric restriction compared to Fasting-Refeeding cycles.
data.authors: Velingkaar N; Astafev AA; Prabahar A; Maravillas MA; Trokhimenko E; Rom JB; Asi GJ; Piontkivska H; Jiang P; Kondratov RV

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Comparing caloric restriction (CR, one meal/day) to a fasting-refeeding-fasting (FRF) regimen with matched food intake and fasting duration, CR engages anticipatory, circadian-clock-aligned metabolic control (hepatic mTOR signaling, ketogenesis, metabolic gene coordination), whereas FRF responses track direct nutrient/gastric-emptying cues and disrupt circadian rhythmicity. CR improved glucose and fatty-acid metabolism; FRF caused glucose intolerance and hepatic fat accumulation.
data.abstract_excerpt: Interest in fasting-based diets to improve metabolic health is growing. Caloric restriction (CR) with one meal per day includes an extended fasting component that contributes to its metabolic and longevity benefits, yet the role of fasting within CR remains unclear. Here, we compare CR with a fasting-refeeding-fasting (FRF) regimen while controlling food intake and fasting duration.

extracted_findings.intervention: Caloric restriction (one meal/day) vs matched fasting-refeeding-fasting (FRF) regimen
extracted_findings.target: Hepatic mTOR signaling, ketogenesis and circadian metabolic gene coordination
extracted_findings.effect: CR engages anticipatory, clock-aligned metabolic control and improves glucose/fatty-acid metabolism, whereas FRF tracks direct nutrient cues and causes glucose intolerance and hepatic steatosis.
